note: Russia's national spirits. The ones with `start` describe the situation on 1 January 2000 and cite sources; the others are granted by Russia's focuses, decisions and events. Values are gameplay estimates.

spirits.name: War in Chechnya
spirits.description: The Second Chechen War, begun in August 1999, ties down federal forces in the North Caucasus.

spirits.name: Aftermath of the 1998 crisis
spirits.description: The ruble devaluation and the debt default that began on 17 August 1998 left the banks weak and savings lost.

spirits.name: Demographic decline
spirits.description: Deaths have exceeded births every year since 1992 and the population is falling.

spirits.name: Soviet-era industry
spirits.description: Much of the industry built for the planned economy is old and uncompetitive after the transition to a market economy.

spirits.name: Energy exporter
spirits.description: Russia holds the world's largest natural gas reserves and is one of the largest exporters of oil and gas.

spirits.name: Nuclear weapon state
spirits.description: Russia inherited the Soviet nuclear arsenal, the world's largest, and is one of the five nuclear-weapon states recognised by the Non-Proliferation Treaty.

source.title: Wikipedia: Russia and weapons of mass destruction

spirits.name: Insurgency in the North Caucasus
spirits.description: Major fighting is over, but attacks continue across the North Caucasus.

spirits.name: Fragile recovery
spirits.description: Growth has returned, but the banks and the public finances are still fragile.

spirits.name: The power vertical
spirits.description: A chain of command from the Kremlin through the federal districts to the regions.

spirits.name: Flat income tax
spirits.description: A single income tax rate, simpler to collect and harder to avoid.

spirits.name: Stabilization fund
spirits.description: Part of the oil revenue is saved in a fund that balances the budget when prices fall.

spirits.name: Sovereign wealth funds
spirits.description: A reserve fund for the budget and a national welfare fund for pensions.

spirits.name: State champions
spirits.description: Large state-controlled companies lead energy, arms and transport.

spirits.name: Special economic zones
spirits.description: Tax breaks and simpler customs for investors in designated zones.

spirits.name: Import substitution
spirits.description: Domestic producers replace imported goods behind trade barriers.

spirits.name: Modernised industry
spirits.description: New plants and machinery have replaced much of the Soviet-era industry.

spirits.name: Contract army
spirits.description: Professional soldiers serve alongside a shorter conscription.

spirits.name: Rearmament programme
spirits.description: A ten-year programme replaces Soviet-era equipment.

spirits.name: Family support
spirits.description: Payments for families with a second child, housing help and longer parental leave.

spirits.name: A healthier nation
spirits.description: Better hospitals and campaigns against smoking and alcohol raise life expectancy.

spirits.name: Science drive
spirits.description: Grants, new research universities and labs bring researchers home.

spirits.name: State planning
spirits.description: Investment is directed by state plans for heavy industry and defence.

spirits.name: Mobilised nation
spirits.description: Universal military training and a war economy under a one-party state.

spirits.name: Open society
spirits.description: Independent courts, a free press and competitive elections.
